messages:
Devon: Heads-up — found a model repo that might be tempting to onboard but has weird redistribution language. repo: https://github.com/epsilon/zephyr-7b. The weights tarball includes a 'BY-NC-REDISTRIBUTE' clause. Can we quantize/host this in Hosted or Dedicated? /cc @Olivia @Miguel
Miguel: Quick q — are the weights original or converted? Converted checkpoints sometimes add extra constraints from the converter or source dataset.
Devon: Repo claims 'converted from research checkpoint by eps-team', license file attached in repo. Snippet: 
```
Redistribution allowed for non-commercial use only. No sublicensing. Derivative binaries permitted only for research and evaluation. Commercial deployment prohibited.
```
Miguel: Oof. From an ML perspective: quantized weights are usually considered derivative artifacts. If hosting or shipping quantized binaries is restricted, that blocks most of our deployment surfaces.
Olivia: If the license is BY-NC + no-sublicense, we cannot make the model available to paying customers. Hosting behind our API likely counts as distribution/service to third parties. Need to confirm exact legal text and provenance.
legal-bot: Automated license scan result: model: zephyr-7b, license flags: [NON_COMMERCIAL, NO_SUBLICENSE, POSSIBLE_NO_DERIVATIVE]. Risk: HIGH. Report: https://legal-reports.internal/scan/zephyr-7b-1832004321
Miguel: Also check dataset provenance. Some research checkpoints include downstream license obligations tied to training data. That can create additional commercial constraints.
Sara: Ops note: if Legal blocks hosting, we should also prevent Dedicated reservations and block bundling in any hosted package. Private on-prem might be OK if the customer brings their own weights and we don't distribute. Need explicit approvals.
Devon: Agree. Proposed immediate actions: 1) pause onboarding, 2) add model to registry with license flag 'non-commercial', 3) avoid publishing quantized artifacts, 4) ask upstream for explicit permission for commercial hosting or a different license. I'll file an intake ticket.
Olivia: Also escalate to Compliance for export-control check. Some 'no-derivative' phrasing can be ambiguous across jurisdictions. I'll draft an email to upstream authors requesting clarification and a grant for commercial hosting or a dual-license.
Miguel: For prioritization: set to low. If a paying customer asks we can consider a funded compliance/legal review + provenance audit. For now don't run broad evals that generate artifacts we might accidentally ship.
Devon: I'll add these checklist items to the intake form: provenance chain (original checkpoint SHA + converter tool SHA), exact license file as checksum, whether dataset has third-party restrictions, any CLA or permission records, permitted uses (research-only vs commercial), allowed modifications (quantization/derivatives).
Olivia: Thanks. One more: log all interactions in the model-intake ticket and tag legal@redwood so we have auditable trail if a customer requests it later. :eyes:
Sara: Ops follow-up: If we do a private POC for a customer who wants to test, require them to self-host the weights and sign a custom agreement stating redwood will not distribute the model artifacts.
Devon: Note to self: block automated optimizer that would create and publish a quantized artifact. We'll keep a local eval copy but mark it ephemeral and never push to artifacts bucket.
Miguel: If anyone wants to run internal perf/latency experiments, do so on a dev VM with isolated storage and a short TTL. Do not move anything to artifact storage or model registry until legal clears.
Olivia: I'll follow up with a short checklist and a recommended template email to request permission from upstream. Will paste here when ready.
Devon: Thanks all — filing the intake ticket now and tagging legal & ops.
(edited)
